    AI Overview
    General
    John Daniel "Dan" Caine is a high-ranking United States Air Force officer who became the 22nd Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff on April 11, 2025. As a former F-16 fighter pilot and CIA Associate Director for Military Affairs, he was nominated by President Trump to lead the military, advocating for "peace through strength". 
    Key Facts and Biography of Gen. Dan Caine: 
    • Birth & Background: Born August 10, 1968, in Elmira, New York; son of USAF Lt. Col. (Ret.) Steve Caine.
    • Education: Graduated from Virginia Military Institute (1990) with a B.S. in Economics, and holds a Master of Arts in Air Warfare from American Military University.
    • Military Career:
      Commissioned in 1990, he is a command pilot with over 2,800 F-16 hours, including 150+ combat hours.
    • Roles: Served as Director of Operations at the CIA, part-time National Guard member (2009-2016), and was a serial entrepreneur and investor.
    • Role as Chairman: Assumed the role of highest-ranking military officer in 2025, specializing in aerial tactics, specialized operations, and white house staff roles.
    • Iran Crisis: In March 2026, he appeared with Defense Secretary Pete Hegesth to address security concerns regarding Iran. 
    Caine's career has included serving as a weapons officer and commanding at various levels before his appointment to the Joint Staff.

    Is Dan Caine a 4 star general?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, Dan Caine was promoted to a
    four-star general upon his confirmation as the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff in April 2025. Previously a retired three-star lieutenant general, Caine was recalled to active service by President Trump, making him the first chair who had not previously served as a four-star officer. 
    Key details regarding Caine's promotion and role include: 
    • Role: He serves as the 22nd Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the highest-ranking military officer in the U.S..
    • Promotion: Caine was promoted from lieutenant general (3-star) to four-star general upon his appointment.
    • Unusual Path:
      He was recalled from retirement, having previously worked as the associate director for military affairs at the CIA until December 2024.
    • Waiver: Because he did not meet the traditional requirement of having previously served as a four-star service chief or combatant commander, a "national interest" waiver was used for his appointment. 
    Caine was confirmed by the Senate in a 60–25 vote in April 2025.
